why: The LORD sent Aaron, Moses' brother, to speak for him because Aaron could speak well.
Aaron went in with Moses and told Pharaoh the LORD's word: let my people go.
Miriam the prophetess was Aaron's sister, and she led the women in song after the sea.
On the mount Moses took Aaron's priestly garments and put them on Eleazar his son, and Aaron died there.
Korah's company rose against Aaron's priesthood, and Moses called Korah to stand before the LORD with Aaron.
Cain rose up against his brother Abel in the field and killed him.
Abel was Adam's son, and after Cain killed him, God gave Adam another son in his place.
Eve bore Cain and then his brother Abel.
Abiathar escaped the slaughter at Nob, fled to David, and told him Saul had killed the priests.
Saul had the LORD's priests killed, and Abiathar alone escaped to tell David.
Abiathar the priest sided with Adonijah and helped him when he tried to become king.
Solomon spared Abiathar's life but sent him home to Anathoth and put him out of the priesthood.
Zadok and Abiathar carried the ark of God back to Jerusalem and stayed there for David.
Abigail, a wise and beautiful woman, was the wife of the harsh and evil Nabal.
After Nabal died, Abigail rode out with David's messengers and became his wife.
When Rehoboam died, his son Abijah reigned in his place.
Abijah stood on Mount Zemaraim and called out to Jeroboam before their battle.
When Abijah died, his son Asa reigned in his place.
Abraham gave Abimelech sheep and oxen, and the two of them made a covenant.
Abraham said Sarah was his sister, so Abimelech king of Gerar took her.
Abimelech found out Rebekah was Isaac's wife and asked why he had called her his sister.
Abimelech looked out a window and saw Isaac with Rebekah, and knew she was his wife.
Gideon's concubine in Shechem bore him a son, and he named him Abimelech.
Abimelech killed his seventy brothers on one stone, but Jotham the youngest hid himself and escaped.
Abishai son of Zeruiah was Joab's brother.
Abishai went with David into Saul's camp and begged David to let him strike Saul.
Joab and his brother Abishai killed Abner because he had killed their brother Asahel.
When Shimei cursed David, Abishai asked to go over and take off his head.
David sent Abishai to chase Sheba son of Bichri before he could escape into a strong city.
Abner son of Ner, Saul's uncle, was the captain of Saul's army.
After Saul died, Abner took Ish-bosheth, Saul's son, and made him king.
Joab took Abner aside in the gate at Hebron and struck him dead to avenge his brother.
Abner promised to gather all Israel to David, and David sent him away in peace.
Abram took Sarai as his wife.
Abraham bound his son Isaac and laid him on the altar, as God had told him.
Abram took Lot, his brother's son, with him when he went into Canaan.
Sarai gave her Egyptian maid Hagar to Abram to be his wife.
Hagar bore Abram a son, and Abram named him Ishmael.
Melchizedek, priest of the most high God, brought bread and wine and blessed Abram.
When Absalom rose up against him, David told his servants to flee Jerusalem quickly.
Absalom had his servants kill Amnon at a feast once he was merry with wine.
Absalom comforted his sister Tamar after Amnon wronged her, and she lived in his house.
Joab thrust three darts through Absalom's heart as he hung alive in the oak.
Absalom sent for Ahithophel, David's counselor, and he joined the growing plot.
Hushai talked Absalom out of Ahithophel's good counsel, so the LORD could bring evil on Absalom.
Joshua told Achan to confess and tell what he had done, hiding nothing.
Achish king of Gath took David in and gave him the town of Ziklag.
Shimei broke his oath and went to Achish in Gath to bring back his runaway servants.
Adam named his wife Eve, because she was the mother of all living.
Adam and his wife Eve had a son, Cain.
Solomon swore that Adonijah would die that day and sent Benaiah, who killed him.
At Solomon's word, Benaiah fell upon Adonijah and killed him.
Adonijah talked with Joab, and Joab followed him and helped him seek the throne.
Adonijah came to Bathsheba, Solomon's mother, asking her to speak to the king for him.
Nathan warned Bathsheba that Adonijah had made himself king, and worked to stop him.
After hearing Paul tell his story, Agrippa said Paul had almost persuaded him to be a Christian.
King Agrippa and Bernice came to Caesarea to greet Festus.
Ahab called Elijah Israel's troubler, but Elijah said Ahab's own Baal worship was the trouble.
No one sold himself to wickedness like Ahab, stirred up by Jezebel his wife.
Naboth would not give Ahab his family's vineyard, and Ahab took it once Naboth was dead.
Micaiah said Ahab would not come back from battle in peace, and Ahab was struck by an arrow and died.
Ahab asked Jehoshaphat to go with him to war at Ramoth-gilead, and Jehoshaphat agreed.
When Ahab died, his son Ahaziah reigned in his place.
Jehoram son of Ahab began to reign over Israel in Samaria.
Esther was brought to King Ahasuerus, and he loved her and made her queen.
Queen Vashti held a feast in King Ahasuerus's house, then refused to come when he called.
When Ahasuerus learned of Haman's plot, he had Haman hanged on the gallows Haman had built for Mordecai.
Mordecai the Jew became second only to King Ahasuerus.
The LORD sent Isaiah out to meet King Ahaz with a word for him.
When Ahaz died, his son Hezekiah reigned in his place.
Ahaz the son of Jotham began to reign over Judah.
Pekah king of Israel came up with the king of Syria and besieged Ahaz in Jerusalem.
Elijah told Ahaziah he would not rise from his bed, and he died according to Elijah's word.
Jehoshaphat king of Judah joined himself with Ahaziah king of Israel, who did very wickedly.
Ahijah tore his garment and promised Jeroboam ten tribes, and the kingdom split to fulfil Ahijah's word.
Ahikam stood by Jeremiah so that he was not handed over to the people to be killed.
The king of Babylon made Gedaliah, son of Ahikam, ruler over the people left in Judah.
Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam, and the other men went together to ask Huldah the prophetess.
David heard Ahithophel had joined Absalom's plot and prayed God would turn his counsel to foolishness.
Hushai told Absalom that Ahithophel's counsel was not good, and his own counsel won.
Amaziah the son of Joash began to reign over Judah.
Jehoash king of Israel defeated Amaziah, took him captive, and broke down Jerusalem's wall.
The people of Judah made Uzziah king in place of his father Amaziah.
Amnon had his sister Tamar bring food to his room, then took hold of her and forced her.
Amnon was David's firstborn son, born in Hebron.
The priest of Bethel told King Jeroboam that Amos foretold his death by the sword.
Peter asked Ananias why he lied to the Holy Ghost, and Ananias fell down dead.
The Lord sent Ananias to lay hands on Saul so he could see again and be filled with the Holy Ghost.
The Lord called Ananias in a vision, and he answered, I am here, Lord.
Andrew first found his own brother Simon and told him they had found the Messiah.
Jesus saw Andrew and his brother fishing and called them to follow Him and fish for men.
Andrew heard John the Baptist speak and followed Jesus.
Philip brought a request to Andrew, and together Andrew and Philip told Jesus.
James and John came with Andrew and his brother Simon into their house.
James and John came with Andrew and his brother Simon into their house.
Aquila heard Apollos speak boldly, took him aside, and explained God's way to him more fully.
Priscilla heard Apollos speak boldly, took him aside, and explained God's way to him more fully.
Paul said he planted and Apollos watered, but God gave the growth.
Aquila, a Jew born in Pontus, had come from Italy with his wife Priscilla.
Paul stayed with Aquila and Priscilla in Corinth and worked with them, for they were all tentmakers.
When Asa died, his son Jehoshaphat reigned in his place.
Athaliah killed the royal family, but young Joash was stolen away and hidden from her.
When Athaliah cried treason, Jehoiada the priest had her brought out and killed.
Balak hired Balaam to curse his enemies, but Balaam blessed them instead.
Deborah told Barak the LORD had given Sisera into his hand, and Barak went down from Mount Tabor.
The LORD routed Sisera and his army before Barak, and Sisera fled on foot.
Barnabas took Saul and brought him to the apostles, telling how he had preached boldly at Damascus.
After parting from Paul, Barnabas took Mark with him and sailed to Cyprus.
The church sent Silas with Paul and Barnabas to Antioch.
Peter, James, and John gave Paul and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship.
James, Peter, and John gave Paul and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship.
Blind Bartimaeus heard Jesus was passing near Jericho and cried out to Him for mercy.
Jeremiah called Baruch, and Baruch wrote down all the words of the LORD as Jeremiah spoke them.
King Jehoiakim burned the scroll, so Baruch wrote all of Jeremiah's words again on a new one.
Bathsheba was the wife of Uriah the Hittite when David first saw her.
After Uriah died, David comforted Bathsheba his wife, and she bore him Solomon.
King Solomon rose to meet his mother Bathsheba, bowed to her, and set her at his right hand.
Nathan warned Bathsheba that Adonijah had made himself king, sent her in to David, and promised to come in after her.
Daniel read that Belshazzar's kingdom was given to the Medes and Persians, and that night Belshazzar was slain.
Belshazzar drank from the temple vessels his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem.
Belshazzar was slain that night, and Darius the Median took his kingdom.
David set his mighty man Benaiah over his guard.
Solomon made Benaiah captain over the whole army in Joab's place.
Benaiah went down with Zadok the priest to bring Solomon to Gihon to be anointed.
Benaiah and Nathan the prophet set Solomon on David's mule and brought him to Gihon.
At Solomon's command, Benaiah went up and killed Joab.
Solomon commanded Benaiah, and he struck down Shimei for breaking his oath.
Joseph fell on his brother Benjamin's neck and wept, and Benjamin wept on his neck.
Jacob would not send his youngest son Benjamin to Egypt, fearing harm would come to him.
Rachel died giving birth to Benjamin, naming him Benoni as she died.
Boaz took Ruth as his wife, and the LORD gave her a son.
Boaz was a wealthy kinsman of Naomi's husband, from the family of Elimelech.
After His arrest, Jesus was led to Caiaphas the high priest, where the council had gathered.
Caiaphas and the high priest's family questioned Peter, who answered them filled with the Holy Ghost.
Eve bore Cain and said she had gotten a man from the LORD.
Joshua and Caleb, two of the spies, tore their clothes and urged Israel to trust the LORD.
Moses sent Caleb from Kadeshbarnea to spy out the land, and Caleb brought back an honest report.
Sent by God to Cornelius's house, Peter was met by Cornelius, who fell at his feet.
Zerubbabel rebuilt the LORD's house as King Cyrus of Persia had commanded.
Jeshua the priest rebuilt the LORD's house as King Cyrus of Persia had commanded.
Rachel's maid Bilhah bore a son, and Rachel named him Dan, saying God had judged her.
Bilhah bore Jacob a son, and Rachel named him Dan.
At Daniel's request the king set his friend Shadrach over the affairs of Babylon.
At Daniel's request the king set his friend Meshach over the affairs of Babylon.
After Daniel told his dream, Nebuchadnezzar made him ruler over the province of Babylon.
Darius cast Daniel to the lions but told him, your God will deliver you.
Pharaoh's daughter took the child as her own son and named him Moses.
The daughter of the Pharaoh who ordered the boys drowned found the baby's ark by the river.
Moses' sister offered to fetch a Hebrew nurse, and Pharaoh's daughter told her to go.
Saul threw his javelin to pin David to the wall, but David escaped twice.
Jonathan's soul was knit with David's, and he loved him as his own soul.
David killed Goliath the Philistine in the valley of Elah and later took up his sword.
Samuel anointed David among his brothers, and the Spirit of the LORD came upon him.
Nathan rebuked David for his sin, saying, Thou art the man.
As David's death drew near, he gave a charge to his son Solomon.
Joab was over the army while David reigned over all Israel.
Saul gave his daughter Michal to David as his wife.
David sent a letter by Uriah's own hand ordering him set where he would be killed.
Saul sent to Jesse asking for his son David, who kept the sheep.
David showed kindness to Mephibosheth for Jonathan's sake and gave him a place at his table.
Hushai, David's friend, went into Jerusalem as Absalom arrived there.
Shimei came out cursing David and threw stones at him as he fled.
David would not take Ornan's threshing floor as a gift, but paid him full price.
Hiram king of Tyre sent cedar trees and builders to make David a house.
David struck down Hadarezer king of Zobah.
As he fled Absalom, David told Zadok to carry the ark back into the city.
Nabal insulted David's servants, asking, Who is David?
When Sheba son of Bichri led Israel away, David sent his men to chase him.
Deborah said the LORD would sell Sisera into the hand of a woman.
Delilah had Samson's hair shaved while he slept, then cried that the Philistines were upon him.
Demetrius stirred up the silversmiths, warning that Paul was turning people away from their idols.
Simeon and Levi, Dinah's brothers, took their swords and killed the men of Shechem's city.
Jacob heard that Shechem had defiled his daughter Dinah.
Leah bore a daughter and named her Dinah.
Peter knelt and prayed and said, Tabitha, arise, and she opened her eyes and sat up.
Moses and Eleazar came down from the mount together after Aaron died.
Eleazar the priest and Joshua divided the land of Canaan among the tribes.
Phinehas, Eleazar's son, rose up with a javelin to stop the plague.
Eli taught young Samuel to answer, Speak, LORD; for thy servant heareth.
Eli thought praying Hannah was drunk, but she told him she had poured out her soul.
Eliakim asked Rabshakeh to speak in Syrian so the people on the wall would not understand.
Eliakim, over Hezekiah's household, came to him with torn clothes and told him Rabshakeh's words.
Hezekiah sent Eliakim in sackcloth to Isaiah the prophet.
Jezebel sent word to Elijah that she would take his life by the next day.
Elijah found Elisha plowing and cast his mantle upon him.
On the mount, Elijah appeared with Moses talking with Jesus.
Moses and Elijah appeared together, talking with Jesus on the mount.
Seeing Elijah on the mount, Peter offered to make three tabernacles.
Elijah's letter warned Jehoram of a sickness of the bowels, and his bowels fell out and he died.
Elisabeth, of the daughters of Aaron, was the wife of the priest Zacharias.
When Mary greeted Elisabeth, the baby leaped in her womb and she was filled with the Holy Ghost.
Elisabeth bore a son, and when others would name him Zacharias, she said, He shall be called John.
Elisha's servant Gehazi lied to him, and Naaman's leprosy came upon him.
Naaman came to Elisha's door, and Elisha sent word to wash in Jordan seven times.
Elisha wept and told Hazael he would be king over Syria, and the next day Hazael reigned.
Elisha sent a young prophet to anoint Jehu king over Israel.
Joash struck the ground three times, so the dying Elisha said he would beat Syria three times, and he did.
Elisha said that only for Jehoshaphat's sake would he give the kings the LORD's word.
Elisha told Ahab's son, the king of Israel, to go to the prophets of his father and mother.
Enoch lived sixty-five years and became the father of Methuselah.
Joseph named his second son Ephraim, for God had made him fruitful in Egypt.
Jacob crossed his hands and laid his right hand on young Ephraim's head.
Jacob blessed the two brothers and set Ephraim before his older brother Manasseh.
Years after the stolen blessing, Esau ran to meet Jacob, embraced him, and they wept.
Esau came in from hunting just after his father Isaac had blessed Jacob.
Rebekah learned that Esau, her elder son, meant to kill Jacob, and sent Jacob away.
Mordecai raised his orphaned cousin Esther as his own daughter.
Esther told the king, The adversary and enemy is this wicked Haman.
The king made Esther queen in Vashti's place.
The LORD told Ezekiel to set his face against Gog of Magog and prophesy against him.
The LORD told Ezekiel to prophesy against Pharaoh king of Egypt, the great dragon of the rivers.
Nehemiah and Ezra the scribe told the weeping people that this day was holy to the LORD.
Felix sent for Paul and trembled as Paul spoke of righteousness and judgment, but he put him off.
After two years Festus took Felix's place, and Felix left Paul bound.
Leah's maid Zilpah bore Jacob a son, and Leah named him Gad.
Zilpah bore Jacob a son, and he was named Gad.
Reuben and Gad were both sons of Jacob, Reuben by Leah and Gad by Leah's maid Zilpah.
The word of the LORD came to Gad, David's seer, to bring David three choices.
Gad told David to build an altar on Ornan's threshing floor.
Paul was brought up at the feet of Gamaliel and taught the law of the fathers.
Jeremiah went to Gedaliah at Mizpah and lived with him among the people left in the land.
Johanan warned Gedaliah that Ishmael was sent to kill him, but Gedaliah did not believe him.
Nebuchadnezzar made Gedaliah ruler over the people left in Judah.
Gehazi ran after Naaman and lied that Elisha had sent him to ask for silver and clothes.
Jotham, the youngest son of Jerubbaal, was the only one who escaped by hiding when Abimelech killed his brothers.
Goliath mocked the army of Saul and dared them to send a man, and Saul and Israel were terrified.
Hosea obeyed the LORD and married Gomer, the daughter of Diblaim, and she bore him a son.
Hagar was Sarai's maid, and when Sarai dealt harshly with her, Hagar ran away into the wilderness.
Hagar bore Abram a son, and he was named Ishmael.
The word of the LORD came through Haggai to Zerubbabel, governor of Judah, about rebuilding the LORD's house.
Through Haggai the LORD told Joshua the high priest to be strong and work, for the LORD was with them.
Haggai and Zechariah prophesied together in Jerusalem and helped the people as they began to rebuild God's house.
Ham saw his father Noah's nakedness and told his brothers, and Noah woke and cursed Ham's son Canaan.
Ham told his brother Shem about their father's shame, and Shem covered Noah without looking.
Ham told his brother Japheth about their father's shame, and Japheth helped cover Noah without looking.
When Mordecai would not bow to him, Haman was furious and plotted to destroy all of Mordecai's people.
Hannah bore a son and named him Samuel, because she had asked him of the LORD.
Joram son of Ahab went to war against Hazael king of Syria and was wounded at Ramah.
When Hazael set out against Jerusalem, Joash sent him the temple's holy things and gold so he would go away.
King Herod sought to find and kill the young child Jesus, so the family had to flee into Egypt.
An angel warned Joseph that Herod would seek the child, so Joseph fled with Jesus and Mary into Egypt by night.
Herod had John the Baptist seized and bound in prison for the sake of Herodias.
Herod questioned Jesus at His trial, then mocked Him, dressed Him in a fine robe and sent Him back to Pilate.
After Jesus was sent between them, Pilate and Herod, once enemies, became friends that same day.
King Herod turned against the church and killed James, the brother of John, with the sword.
Herod put Peter in prison, but the Lord sent an angel and set Peter free from Herod's hand.
When Hezekiah was sick, Isaiah came to him with the LORD's word to set his house in order.
Rabshakeh stood outside Jerusalem and mocked King Hezekiah's trust in the LORD on behalf of Assyria's king.
Hezekiah's son Manasseh became king and rebuilt the high places his father had torn down.
King Josiah commanded Hilkiah the high priest to clear out of the temple everything made for Baal.
There was peace between Hiram and Solomon, and the two kings made a league together.
Hoshea plotted against King Pekah, struck him down and reigned in his place.
Hushai told Zadok the priest what Ahithophel had advised, so word could be carried to David.
Hushai told Abiathar the priest what Ahithophel had advised, so word could be carried to David.
Isaac brought Rebekah into his mother's tent, and she became his wife, and he loved her.
Jacob came near his blind father Isaac with hairy hands, and Isaac blessed him thinking he was Esau.
Sarah bore Abraham a son in their old age, and he was named Isaac.
Isaac and Ishmael, Abraham's sons, buried their father together in the cave of Machpelah.
Ish-bosheth's killers brought his head to David at Hebron, calling him David's enemy who sought his life.
When David demanded his wife Michal back, Ish-bosheth took her from her husband Phaltiel.
Ish-bosheth was the son of Saul, made king by Saul's captain after his father's death.
Sarah saw Hagar's son mocking and told Abraham to cast out the bondwoman and her son.
When Laban chased him down, Jacob grew angry and argued with Laban over how he had been treated.
Jacob loved Rachel and offered to serve her father seven years to marry her.
Jacob asked for his promised wife, but Laban brought him Leah instead on the wedding night.
Jacob loved Joseph more than all his sons and made him a coat of many colours.
Rebekah told her son Jacob what Isaac had said to Esau and urged him to obey her plan.
Joseph brought his father Jacob before Pharaoh, and Jacob blessed Pharaoh.
Judah begged his father Jacob to send Benjamin with him, promising to bear the blame if harm came.
James and his brother John were mending nets with their father Zebedee when Jesus called them.
Jesus saw James mending nets and called him, and he left his father's boat to follow Jesus.
James and John were fishing partners with Simon Peter when Jesus called them to catch men.
In His hometown the people asked if Jesus was not the brother of James and the son of Mary.
James was named among the sons of Mary when the people of Nazareth spoke of Jesus' family.
Freed from prison, Peter told the believers to go and tell James what the Lord had done.
When Paul came to Jerusalem, he went in to see James, with all the elders there.
Japheth was one of the three sons of Noah who came out of the ark.
Japheth and his brother Shem laid a garment on their shoulders and walked backward to cover their father.
When Jehoiakim died, his son Jehoiachin reigned in his place.
Nebuchadnezzar besieged Jerusalem, and Jehoiachin went out to him and was taken captive.
After Jehoiachin was taken away, Babylon's king made his uncle Mattaniah king in his place, renaming him Zedekiah.
Joash did right in the LORD's sight all the days that Jehoiada the priest taught him.
Pharaoh made Josiah's son Eliakim king in his father's place and changed his name to Jehoiakim.
Jehoiakim burned the scroll of Jeremiah's words, so the LORD told Jeremiah to write it all again.
Nebuchadnezzar made Jehoiakim his servant for three years, and then Jehoiakim rebelled against him.
Jehoshaphat gave his sons rich gifts, but he gave the kingdom to Jehoram because he was the firstborn.
Jehoram married Ahab's daughter and walked in the evil ways of Ahab's house.
Jehoshaphat asked for a true prophet of the LORD, and Micaiah was named, though the king of Israel hated him.
King Jehoram of Israel asked Jehoshaphat to go with him against Moab, and Jehoshaphat agreed.
Jehu drew his bow with all his strength and shot King Joram through the heart.
When Jehu came to Jezreel, Jezebel mocked him from a window, and he had her thrown down.
Jehu struck down everyone left of Ahab's house in Jezreel, until none remained.
Jehu had Joram's body thrown into Naboth's field, repaying the blood of Naboth as the LORD had said.
King Zedekiah secretly asked Jeremiah for a word from the LORD, and Jeremiah said he would be given to Babylon.
Nebuchadnezzar ordered his captain to look after Jeremiah well and do him no harm.
Johanan and the proud men told Jeremiah he was lying when he warned them not to go to Egypt.
Solomon tried to kill Jeroboam, so Jeroboam fled to Egypt until Solomon died.
There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all their days.
When Jehoash king of Israel died, his son Jeroboam reigned in his place.
Jeroboam won back Israel's borders just as the LORD had spoken through the prophet Jonah.
The LORD sent Samuel to Jesse the Bethlehemite, for He had chosen a king among Jesse's sons.
King Saul asked Jesse to send him David, and Jesse sent David to Saul with bread, wine and a kid.
Jesus saw Simon Peter casting a net by the sea of Galilee and called him to follow and fish for men.
Jesus called John and his brother James from their father's ship, and they left Zebedee and followed Him.
Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan so that John could baptize Him.
Jesus found Philip as He set out for Galilee and told him, Follow me.
Jesus saw Matthew sitting at the tax booth and said, Follow me, and Matthew rose and followed Him.
The risen Jesus told doubting Thomas to touch His hands and side, and Thomas cried, My Lord and my God.
Pilate questioned Jesus, and when the crowd cried for His death, he handed Him over to be crucified.
Mary gave birth to her firstborn son Jesus in Bethlehem and laid Him in a manger.
Joseph obeyed the angel, took Mary as his wife, and named her son Jesus.
Jesus loved Martha of Bethany, along with her sister and Lazarus.
Mary of Bethany sat at the feet of Jesus and listened to His word.
Jesus stood at the tomb of His friend Lazarus and cried with a loud voice, Lazarus, come forth.
At the empty tomb the risen Jesus called Mary Magdalene by name, and she answered, Rabboni, Master.
On the high mountain Moses appeared and talked with Jesus as He was transfigured.
Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews, came to Jesus by night and called Him a teacher come from God.
Jesus looked up into the tree and told Zacchaeus to come down, for He would stay at his house.
When Jesus was brought to the temple as a baby, Simeon took Him in his arms and blessed God.
On the road to Damascus Jesus spoke to Saul from heaven and asked why he was persecuting Him.
As he was about to be stoned, Stephen looked into heaven and saw Jesus standing at God's right hand.
Moses kept the flock of his father-in-law Jethro, and later took his advice to share the work of judging.
When Jethro offered sacrifices to God, Aaron and the elders came to eat bread with him.
Jezebel had Naboth stoned, then told Ahab to go and take his vineyard.
When Joram asked Jehu for peace, Jehu answered that there could be none while his mother Jezebel's sins went on.
Joab set Uriah where the bravest enemy fighters were, and Uriah the Hittite was killed.
Joab besieged the city where Sheba hid, until its people cut off Sheba's head and threw it out to him.
When Joab fled to the altar, King Solomon sent Benaiah to fall upon him.
Joab and Abiathar the priest together followed Adonijah and helped him.
Johanan and the proud men accused Baruch of turning Jeremiah against them.
The angel told Zacharias that his wife Elisabeth would bear him a son named John.
Peter and John went up together to the temple at the hour of prayer.
John, with James and Peter, gave Paul the right hand of fellowship.
Saul threw a javelin at his own son Jonathan, and Jonathan knew his father meant to kill David.
Jonathan's son Mephibosheth was five when news came of his father's death, and he fell and became lame.
Pharaoh set Joseph over all the land of Egypt.
Judah talked his brothers out of killing Joseph and into selling him to the Ishmeelites.
Reuben saved his brother Joseph from being killed and had him put in a pit instead.
Joseph named his firstborn son Manasseh, for God had made him forget all his toil.
Potiphar bought Joseph as a slave, saw the LORD was with him, and made him overseer of his house.
Rachel gave birth to Joseph and prayed the LORD would add another son.
Mary, the mother of Jesus, was engaged to Joseph.
In the temple Simeon blessed Joseph and Mary and spoke of what the child would be.
Moses laid his hands on Joshua before the people and gave him a charge to lead them.
Joshua saved Rahab and her household alive, because she had hidden the spies he sent to Jericho.
Joshua and Zerubbabel stood up with their brethren and built the altar of the God of Israel.
Zechariah prophesied, and Joshua and Zerubbabel rose up to build the house of God with the prophets helping.
When Josiah died, Jeremiah lamented for him.
When the LORD struck King Uzziah with leprosy, his son Jotham took charge of the palace and judged the people.
Judah and Benjamin were both sons of Jacob, Judah by Leah and Benjamin by Rachel.
Judah admitted that his daughter-in-law Tamar was more righteous than he, for he had kept his son from her.
Judah was one of the sons Leah bore to Jacob.
Judas led a crowd to Jesus and betrayed Him with a kiss.
Korah and his followers rose up against Moses, and Moses answered him before the LORD.
Laban made a wedding feast and in the evening brought his daughter Leah to Jacob.
Rachel hid her father Laban's household idols and sat on them while he searched the tent.
Rebekah's brother Laban ran out to meet Abraham's servant at the well.
Lazarus of Bethany, who fell sick, was the brother of Mary and her sister Martha.
Mary, who anointed the Lord, was the sister of Lazarus when he was sick.
Leah and her sister Rachel quarrelled over the mandrakes and over Jacob.
Leah named her firstborn Reuben, hoping her husband would now love her.
When others had left, Luke alone stayed with Paul.
Paul named Mark and Luke together as his fellow workers.
The Lord opened Lydia's heart to Paul's words, and after her baptism she welcomed him into her home.
Israel laid his left hand on Manasseh's head and his right on his younger brother Ephraim's.
Samson was buried in the burying place of Manoah his father.
Barnabas and Saul took John Mark with them when they returned from Jerusalem.
Freed from prison, Peter went to the house of Mark's mother, where many were praying.
Martha complained that her sister Mary had left her to serve alone while Mary sat at Jesus' feet.
Simeon blessed the family and told Mary that her child was set for the fall and rising of many.
Mary the mother of Jesus and Mary Magdalene stood together by the cross.
When Mary anointed Jesus' feet with costly ointment, Judas Iscariot complained it should have been sold for the poor.
Mary Magdalene found the tomb open and ran to tell Simon Peter that the Lord had been taken away.
Meshach and Shadrach stood together and would not serve Babylon's gods or bow to the golden image.
Furious that Meshach would not bow, Nebuchadnezzar had the furnace heated seven times hotter and had him thrown in.
Saul turned on his daughter Michal for deceiving him and helping David escape.
Miriam was the sister of Moses.
Moses went to Pharaoh with the LORD's word: Let my people go.
When Pharaoh heard Moses had killed an Egyptian, he sought to kill him, and Moses fled to Midian.
Naomi came home to Bethlehem with Ruth, her daughter-in-law from Moab.
Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anointed Solomon king at Gihon.
Nathan and Zadok the priest stood together and brought Solomon to Gihon to be made king.
Nebuchadnezzar raged at Shadrach for refusing to bow and heated the furnace seven times hotter.
Zedekiah fled, was caught on the plains of Jericho, and was brought to Nebuchadnezzar for judgment.
Sanballat tried to lure Nehemiah out to the plain of Ono, meaning to do him harm.
Tobiah sent letters to frighten Nehemiah and stop the work on the wall.
Shem honored his father Noah by covering him with a garment, walking in backward.
Paul led Onesimus to faith while in chains and called him his own son.
Beaten and locked in prison, Paul and Silas prayed and sang praises at midnight.
Paul met the young disciple Timothy at Lystra and took him along on his journeys.
Paul called Titus his own son in the faith.
When Stephen was stoned, the witnesses laid their clothes at the feet of a young man named Saul.
Paul greeted Priscilla as one of his helpers in Christ Jesus.
Three years after his conversion, Paul went up to Jerusalem to see Peter and stayed with him fifteen days.
Festus asked Paul to stand trial in Jerusalem, but Paul said he stood at Caesar's judgment seat.
On his way to Jerusalem, Paul stayed at the house of Philip the evangelist in Caesarea.
When Simon offered money for the power of the Holy Ghost, Peter said, Thy money perish with thee.
Potiphar was Pharaoh's officer, the captain of the guard.
Philip and Stephen were chosen together among the seven to serve the church.
Simon the sorcerer believed, was baptized, and stayed close to Philip, amazed at the signs.
Phinehas, grandson of Aaron the priest, stopped the plague by his zeal for God.
Moses sent Phinehas to the war against Midian with the holy instruments and trumpets.
The queen of Sheba heard of Solomon's fame and came to test him with hard questions.
Rahab was the mother of Boaz, born to her and Salmon.
Rehoboam reigned in his father Solomon's place when Solomon died.
Jacob told his firstborn Reuben he would not excel, because he had defiled his father's bed.
Samuel told Saul that because he rejected the LORD's word, the LORD had rejected him as king.
Sanballat and Tobiah joined together to mock and oppose the rebuilding of Jerusalem's wall.
Solomon told Shimei the LORD would repay his wickedness against David, and had him put to death.
Moses and Israel struck down Sihon king of the Amorites and took his land.
Silas and Timotheus stayed behind together at Berea when Paul was sent away.
Jacob scolded his sons Simeon and Levi for the trouble their revenge on Shechem brought him.
Joseph took his brother Simeon and bound him before their eyes, keeping him in Egypt.
Leah bore Simeon, saying the LORD had heard that she was hated.
King David sent his daughter Tamar to Amnon's house to make him food.
Four sons of the giant in Gath fell by the hand of David and his servants.
When the giant's son Ishbibenob tried to kill David, Abishai came to his help and killed him.
Thomas was with Simon Peter and other disciples by the sea when the risen Jesus appeared.
Titus went up to Jerusalem with Paul and Barnabas.
Isaiah the prophet wrote down the acts of Uzziah from first to last.
Mary came into the house of Zacharias and greeted Elisabeth.
Zadok the priest took the horn of oil from the tabernacle and anointed Solomon king.
The LORD gave Zechariah a word for Zerubbabel: not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit.
Ehud came to King Eglon with a secret message from God and killed him with a dagger.
Eliphaz was one of Job's three friends who came to mourn with him and comfort him.
Bildad was one of Job's three friends who came to mourn with him and comfort him.
Zophar was one of Job's three friends who came to mourn with him and comfort him.
Elihu waited until Job had spoken, then grew angry because Job justified himself rather than God.
Eliphaz and Bildad made an appointment together to come and comfort Job.
Eliphaz and Zophar made an appointment together to come and comfort Job.
Bildad and Zophar made an appointment together to come and comfort Job.
Elihu was angry with Job's three friends because they found no answer, yet had condemned Job.
Elihu was angry with Job's three friends because they found no answer, yet had condemned Job.
Elihu was angry with Job's three friends because they found no answer, yet had condemned Job.
Micah hired the young Levite as his own priest for ten shekels a year, clothes and food.
Gilead was Jephthah's father, and his wife's sons drove Jephthah out of their father's house.
Malachi promised that Elijah would come, and Jesus said John the Baptist was that Elias.
Isaiah foretold a voice crying in the wilderness to prepare the LORD's way, and John the Baptist was that voice.
Jesus read Isaiah's words about the One anointed to preach good tidings and said they were fulfilled that day.
Isaiah named Cyrus as the LORD's shepherd who would say Jerusalem shall be built, and Cyrus was charged to build the LORD's house.
The LORD told Elijah that Jehu would be king and strike Ahab's house, and Jehu did, as spoken to Elijah.
Ezekiel said the prince would be taken to Babylon yet not see it, and Zedekiah's eyes were put out before Babylon.
Jeremiah said Coniah and his mother would be cast out to Babylon, and Jehoiachin and his mother were carried there.
Jeremiah foretold Rachel weeping for her children, and it was fulfilled when Herod killed the children of Bethlehem.
Nathan warned that David's wives would be taken openly by another, and Absalom went in to them before all Israel.
Peter said the Holy Ghost spoke by David about Judas, that another should take his office.
David wrote that God's Holy One would not see corruption, and Peter said David, a prophet, spoke of Christ's resurrection.
After a night of prayer, Jesus chose Bartholomew as one of His twelve apostles.
Jesus chose James the son of Alphaeus as one of His twelve apostles.
Judas, not Iscariot, asked Jesus how He would show Himself to them and not to the world.
Jesus chose Simon called Zelotes as one of His twelve apostles.
Joseph of Arimathaea was a disciple of Jesus, and he laid Jesus' body in his own new tomb.
Joseph went in boldly to Pilate and asked for Jesus' body, and Pilate gave it to him.
Joseph and Nicodemus wrapped Jesus' body in linen with spices and buried Him together.
Simon of Cyrene was made to carry the cross behind Jesus.
The crowd asked for Barabbas to be released, and Jesus was handed over to be crucified.
Pilate, wanting to please the crowd, released Barabbas to them.
Herod married Herodias, his brother Philip's wife.
Herodias held a grudge against John the Baptist and would have killed him.
Ananias and his wife Sapphira sold land together and kept back part of the price.
Peter asked Sapphira why she had agreed to tempt the Spirit of the Lord, and she fell down dead.
Annas was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, the high priest that year.
Jesus was led bound to Annas first, and Annas sent Him bound to Caiaphas.
Annas and the high priest's family questioned Peter about the power by which a man was healed.
Paul wrote to Philemon as his dearly beloved fellow worker.
Paul sent Onesimus back to Philemon, asking him to receive him as a beloved brother.
Abednego and Shadrach answered the king together and would not serve his gods.
Abednego and Meshach came out of the fiery furnace together, unharmed.
Daniel told his companion Azariah about the king's secret so they could pray to God for mercy.
Nebuchadnezzar had Abednego bound and thrown into the burning fiery furnace.
Jael drove a tent nail through the sleeping Sisera and killed him.
Jael met Barak as he chased Sisera and showed him Sisera lying dead in her tent.
The song Deborah sang that day called Jael blessed above women for killing Sisera.
Seth was Adam's son, born in his likeness, after his image.
Eve bore Seth and said God had given her another seed instead of Abel.
Seth was given to Eve in place of his brother Abel, whom Cain killed.
The priest of Midian gave his daughter Zipporah to Moses as his wife.
Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, brought his daughter Zipporah back to Moses in the wilderness.
Othniel was Caleb's younger brother, and Caleb gave him his daughter Achsah for taking Kirjath-sepher.
Simeon and Levi, brothers of Dinah, took their swords and killed the men of Shechem.
Leah bore Levi, her third son, hoping her husband would be joined to her.
Jacob rebuked his sons Simeon and Levi for bringing trouble on him at Shechem.
Levi and Simeon, Dinah's brothers, took her out of Shechem's house.
Leah bore Issachar and said God had given her her hire.
Leah traded Reuben's mandrakes for the night Issachar was conceived.
Leah bore Zebulun, her sixth son, and said now her husband would dwell with her.
Issachar and Zebulun were both sons of Leah, born one after the other.
Rachel named Naphtali, saying she had wrestled with her sister and won.
Dan and Naphtali were the two sons of Bilhah, Rachel's maid.
Leah named Asher, saying the daughters would call her blessed.
Gad and Asher were the two sons of Zilpah, Leah's maid.
Joel said the LORD would pour out His spirit on all flesh, and at Pentecost Peter said this was what Joel had spoken.
Obadiah's vision was against Edom, the mount of Esau, for the violence Esau's people did to their brother Jacob.
Micah told Judah in Hezekiah's day that Zion would be plowed like a field, and Hezekiah feared the LORD and sought Him.
Ahaziah's mother Athaliah was his counsellor to do evil.
When Jehoram died, his son Ahaziah reigned over Judah in his place.
Jehu chased Ahaziah and had him struck down in his chariot.
Ahaziah went to war with Joram against Syria, then went down to Jezreel to see him when he was wounded.
Joash was Ahaziah's son, stolen away and hidden when Athaliah killed the royal family.
Amon was Manasseh's son and served the idols his father had made.
After Amon was killed, the people made his son Josiah king.
When Josiah was killed, the people anointed his son Jehoahaz king in his place.
Pharaoh-nechoh took Jehoahaz to Egypt and made his brother Eliakim king, renaming him Jehoiakim.
